body.statement: The total interval \(C_\alpha\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies \[\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]\le CR_\star^{1/2}.\] Every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_\star^{1/2}\). The retained-block coupling error obeys \(M\beta_0\rho_0^{g_T}=o(1)\); the block jackknife/Rademacher law consistently estimates the calendar fluctuation; and the event Rademacher law handles the bounded, conditionally independent, nonidentically distributed finite-cohort summands. Under the donor replication and covariance assumptions, the \(Y_j\) are independent with \(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^{\top}\mid E_0]=I_D\), and \(\mathbb E_P[\|m_k^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le M_4(m_k)\) implies \(P\{\max_k\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0)\|_2>\delta_k\mid E_0\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) by Markov's inequality and a union bound. Separate calibration of the calendar and event components introduces no event/history independence assumption, and Bonferroni over the three error allocations gives coverage. Discarded gaps are \(o(T)\), \(M\to\infty\), selected-Gram failures have vanishing probability at the required order, \(A_L=O_P((R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{1/2})\), \(A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(N^{-\kappa/2})\), and \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}+r_{\mathrm{tr}}=O_P((R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{1/2}+R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2})\). The bounds therefore hold for every relative growth regime without undersmoothing, an extra deconvolution term, or a multiplicative logarithmic phase.
body.justification: Risk optimality alone does not guarantee honest conditional uncertainty quantification at phase boundaries.
body.gap: Armstrong--Kolesar use a fixed Gaussian operator and Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik treat constrained linear prediction; neither establishes expected-length optimality for this moving-center product experiment.
body.consumer: Event-study confidence intervals remain valid when calendar overlap, donor covariance estimation, and nonparametric bias are simultaneously first order.
